title: She Sells Seashells
subtitle: Sibilant S & SH
description: This exercise trains your ability to switch rapidly between the /s/ and /ʃ/ (SH) sounds. Mastering the distinction prevents the two sounds from blurring together under speed.
tip: Keep your tongue tip behind your lower teeth for /s/, then pull it back and raise it for /ʃ/ — feel the shift before each word.
phrases: She sells seashells by the seashore.
The shells she sells are surely seashells.
So if she sells shells on the seashore, I'm sure she sells seashore shells.
Sally sells short silk shirts, surely she ships some silk.
Shy Shelly says she shall sew sheets.
Six slick slim slippery slithering snakes sat silently.
